'''Neal Lloyd First''' (October 8, 1930 – November 20, 2014) was an American [[biologist]].<ref name=nasm>{{cite web|title=Neal L. First|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/neal-l-first-nn2po9/|website=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=12 June 2015}}</ref>

== Birth and education ==
Neal L. First was born in 1930.<ref name=nasm />

== Awards and honors ==
Neal L. First received several awards. He received the Animal Science Morrison Award, the Upjohn Research Award, the Society for the Study of Reproduction Research Award, the National Association of Animal Breeders Research Award and the Von Humboldt Award. In 1996/7, he received the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]] "for his pioneering research in the reproductive biology of livestock".<ref>{{cite web | url = https://wolffund.org.il/2018/12/10/neal-l-first/ | title = Neal L. First - Wolf Foundation | website = [[Wolf Foundation]] | accessdate = September 8, 2020}}</ref> He was at the faculty of the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] when he received the prize.

He was also a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=nasm />

== Personal life ==

First died on November 20, 2014, from cancer, but surrounded by loving family.<ref>{{cite web|title=In memoriam: Neal L. First, pioneer in reproductive physiology|url=http://ecals.cals.wisc.edu/2014/11/24/in-memoriam-neal-l-first-pioneering-scientist-in-genetics-and-agriculture/|website=[[University of Wisconsin]] college of Agriculture and Life Sciences|via=ecals.cals.wisc.edu|accessdate=June 12, 2015}}</ref>
